W: Matteo, do you have time to help me organize the storage room? The construction crew's going to be starting renovations on the lobby next week. We need to make space to store the lobby furniture.

W: Hi, Liam. We're really glad to have you join our team. The harvest season is our busiest!
M1: I'm excited to get started.
W: Let me introduce you to Brian. He will take you out to the berry fields for your training.
M2: Hi, Liam. Here's a pair of gloves for you to use.
M1: Thanks!
M2: The berry picking is really straightforward. But it's important that you get plenty of water and stay hydrated in this heat.
M1: I brought a big bottle of it with me, so I should be fine.

M: Welcome to my gardening podcast. I'm Rajesh Varma, and today I'm here with So-Jin Lee, a botanist from Denton University who recently developed a new hybrid flower. Could you tell us more, Professor Lee?
W: Certainly. I developed a new type of rose—it's special because it blooms longer than any other rose.
M: That's interesting. Is it difficult to grow?
W: Not if it's planted under the right conditions. Next month, the rose will be featured at the botanical show downtown. I hope your listeners will come to see it.

W: So, Vivek, I think our employees could benefit from some more training. How about using this software application that I found? The app provides a platform for uploading our own training videos. And employees could view them on their phones at any time.
M: You know, I've heard that those online programs help employees retain knowledge. But aren't those apps expensive?
W: Actually, the cost is reasonable. And the Web site has some interesting reviews from other businesses that have used the app and found it helpful.

M: Hi, Christina. Did you have a chance to look over the applications from our sales representatives who are interested in the new team leader role? We'll need to decide on a team leader soon.
W: I did. I really liked Amanda Diop's application. She's the one who signed that deal with Wallerston Corporation.
M: I agree. That was an impressive deal. Wallerston is one of our biggest clients now. I think Amanda would be a great choice.
W: OK. I'm glad we're on the same page. I'll complete the paperwork and send it to the human resources department later today.

W1: Thanks for agreeing to this interview for our upcoming article in the Thomasville Gazette, Ms. Haddad.
W2: Of course. As you know, the city council is proposing the implementation of a road tax. And I want to make sure the public is informed about it.
M: Well, we like to keep our readers in the know, so we have a long list of questions for you.
W1: I'll start. What does the city plan to do with this tax revenue, Ms. Haddad?
W2: The money will be used to add bicycle lanes citywide, which I'm excited about. Bicycle lanes should reduce traffic and promote health.
M: Some business owners are concerned about losing street parking. Are you worried about that?

M: Good morning, Ms. Gomez. I wanted to update you on the travel plans for your meeting with Scarney Department Store.
W: Thanks for taking care of that. They're prospective clients, and I've been so busy sending them samples and preparing my presentation that I haven't given a thought to my reservations.
M: Happy to help. I've confirmed your plane reservation. Just remember, Vela Air only allows one free piece of carry-on luggage. Otherwise, there'll be an extra charge.
W: OK. Can you forward the plane ticket confirmation, please?
M: I'll e-mail you right now.

M: Hi. I'm Marcel from Novik Solutions. Glad you could stop by my trade show booth today.
W: Nice to meet you. I'm Silvia from Media Futurescapes. So what type of product does your company provide?
M: We create accounting software so that companies can do their own accounting. Currently, I'm showcasing a new version for companies with under 50 employees.
W: Well, we have about 200 employees.
M: I understand. Here's a chart that provides an overview of our complete range of products.

W: Rodrigo, aren't we scheduled to start the seal-coating job for the street parking around Bevelton Shopping Center next week?
M: We were going to start those repairs on Monday, but I've been looking at the weather; it's going to rain all weekend. I think we should reschedule.
W: Right. We can't add a protective layer to the asphalt when it's wet. I'll contact the property manager at the shopping center to discuss alternative dates.
M: OK. Just so you know, we've received a few new requests for consultations on our road repair services. I'll try to slot those in for Monday instead.

M: Tasnim, I've been looking at the production process for soaps in our facility, and I think there's room for improvement.
W: Improvements that could decrease our production time?
M: Yes. Consider this: once the soap mixtures are poured into the molds, employees have to carry the batches across the room.
W: I see what you mean. If we reinstalled the drying racks closer to the mixing station, they wouldn't have to walk as far.
M: Exactly. A small change like that can have a big effect on total output.
W: But wouldn't that be expensive?
M: Let me show you the cost projection.

M: I was just looking at the supply request form you submitted for our engineering department.
W: Yes?
M: I think you might've made a mistake. Do we really need that many computer mouses?
W: Oh, that is a mistake! I meant to request two.
M: OK, great. I did think that was strange, given that there are only fifteen of us in our department!
W: Thanks for catching that. Do you know when the supplies will get here?
M: I'll place the order this afternoon, so they'll probably arrive next week.

W: Welcome to Halcyon Florals. How can I help you?
M: Hi. I'm planning the Lambert-Evans wedding that's taking place this weekend. I received an e-mail this morning that there's a problem with the flowers I ordered for the floral arrangements.
W: Yes, unfortunately, my supplier notified me that they're out of stock because of a shortage. I'm sorry, but you'll have to choose a replacement for the lilies.
M: I know my client likes orchids, but I'm guessing those are too expensive. We'll still need a flower that's under five dollars per stem.
W: Well, what about these? They fit within your budget.
M: Those will be perfect.

W: I think I've inspected enough to determine a fair market value for your store.
M: OK. You have the paperwork verifying that I replaced my roof last year, right? Buyers look for properties that don't need major repairs.
W: I do have that. And you're right—recent repairs are a factor that add to the value of a property.
M: The historic windows will be a selling point, I think. They're made of handblown glass. All the storefronts in this row of shops have them.

Book Review: Leadership: Essays on Being a Great Leader

As a businessperson, I am glad there is a publisher whose sole focus is on business. Skymill Publishing's latest book is a great one for leaders in all industries. Joan Cristophe has sought out some of the world's best minds to write essays for this book that will provide readers with some unique perspectives. In her own introduction, she argues that there is a greater need than ever before for more effective leaders in business.

Cristophe expertly arranges the essays in this collection so that the voices of each author complement one another. The essay by Xiaofeng Li is the perfect example of this. It is strategically sandwiched between Francisca Conde's essay on leadership in action and Ron Blake's essay on focusing on the details. Roderick Muller's essay is the sole disappointment. Surprisingly little new information or insight is offered on its pages, and the writing style is rather flat. Besides that, the collection is excellent, and readers with an interest in leadership in many different situations will find useful nuggets of wisdom and vision within.

Hiking Permits to Be Required for Upton Parks

UPTON (January 8)—Starting on May 25, hikers will be required to obtain a permit for each day they hike on certain trails in Upton parks. The designated trails include some of the most popular hiking spots in the area. The permits are free of charge and require only that hikers register online at www.uptonparks.org or at any Upton Parks Department office. Upon registering, hikers will receive a permit that they can print out or display on a mobile device.

The move is part of an effort to reduce foot traffic on the most used trails, but some hikers are concerned. "I might not be able to get a permit for my favorite trails if none are left when I want to go," says Regina Faroni, an Upton parks hiker. "In addition, I often check the weather in the morning and then decide if it is a good day to hike," she says. Having to apply for a permit could prevent her from taking spontaneous hikes. "On the other hand, it would reduce the number of hikers on certain trails," Faroni admits.

—EJ Harjo, Upton Digest

To: Upton Parks Department <info@uptonparks.org>

Subject: Hiking permits

Date: January 22

To Whom It May Concern,

I read in the Upton Digest that hikers soon will be required to register for permits to hike on certain trails. As the organizer of the Upton Hiking Club, I would like more details on how this will affect our club. For example, is there a list of hiking trails that will require permits? I checked your Web site and could not find one.

Is it also the case that the number of permits issued will vary from trail to trail? About seventeen to twenty club members participate in our group hikes. I'm concerned that we may not get enough permits to hike together. Are there special considerations for large groups?

Finally, I am concerned that the permit requirement will not allow our club members to get together for a hike on the spur of the moment. We often will take an unplanned hike if we find that several members have a free day.

I hope you are able to respond soon, as we are already planning our spring and summer hikes.

Regards,

Arlo Gomes
Organizer, Upton Hiking Club

From: Upton Parks Department <info@uptonparks.org>

Permits can be reserved up to two weeks in advance, and the number of permits available for most trails is substantially higher than the number of Upton Hiking Club members who join your group hikes. Same-day permits can be obtained.

If you have not already done so, you can sign up on our Web site for our weekly newsletter. Doing so will ensure that you get advance notice of any updates to our policies.

Jenny Grieb, Public Relations, Upton Parks Department

Skymill Publishing

Joan Cristophe, Senior Editor

Table of Contents

Introduction — ii

Beyond the Meeting Agenda: Leadership in Action — 2
Francisca Conde

Xiaofeng Li

Think Small...Details Matter — 51
Ron Blake

Low-Tech Managers in Business — 83
T. Walker Prince

Future Leadership Models — 119
Roderick Muller

Book Review: Leadership: Essays on Being a Great Leader

As a businessperson, I am glad there is a publisher whose sole focus is on business. Skymill Publishing's latest book is a great one for leaders in all industries. Joan Cristophe has sought out some of the world's best minds to write essays for this book that will provide readers with some unique perspectives. In her own introduction, she argues that there is a greater need than ever before for more effective leaders in business.

Cristophe expertly arranges the essays in this collection so that the voices of each author complement one another. The essay by Xiaofeng Li is the perfect example of this. It is strategically sandwiched between Francisca Conde's essay on leadership in action and Ron Blake's essay on focusing on the details. Roderick Muller's essay is the sole disappointment. Surprisingly little new information or insight is offered on its pages, and the writing style is rather flat. Besides that, the collection is excellent, and readers with an interest in leadership in many different situations will find useful nuggets of wisdom and vision within.

questions.passage_text:
Hiking Permits to Be Required for Upton Parks

UPTON (January 8)—Starting on May 25, hikers will be required to obtain a permit for each day they hike on certain trails in Upton parks. The designated trails include some of the most popular hiking spots in the area. The permits are free of charge and require only that hikers register online at www.uptonparks.org or at any Upton Parks Department office. Upon registering, hikers will receive a permit that they can print out or display on a mobile device.

The move is part of an effort to reduce foot traffic on the most used trails, but some hikers are concerned. "I might not be able to get a permit for my favorite trails if none are left when I want to go," says Regina Faroni, an Upton parks hiker. "In addition, I often check the weather in the morning and then decide if it is a good day to hike," she says. Having to apply for a permit could prevent her from taking spontaneous hikes. "On the other hand, it would reduce the number of hikers on certain trails," Faroni admits.

—EJ Harjo, Upton Digest

From: Arlo Gomes <arlog@uptonhikingclub.org>

To: Upton Parks Department <info@uptonparks.org>

Subject: Hiking permits

Date: January 22

To Whom It May Concern,

I read in the Upton Digest that hikers soon will be required to register for permits to hike on certain trails. As the organizer of the Upton Hiking Club, I would like more details on how this will affect our club. For example, is there a list of hiking trails that will require permits? I checked your Web site and could not find one.

Is it also the case that the number of permits issued will vary from trail to trail? About seventeen to twenty club members participate in our group hikes. I'm concerned that we may not get enough permits to hike together. Are there special considerations for large groups?

Finally, I am concerned that the permit requirement will not allow our club members to get together for a hike on the spur of the moment. We often will take an unplanned hike if we find that several members have a free day.

I hope you are able to respond soon, as we are already planning our spring and summer hikes.

Regards,

Arlo Gomes
Organizer, Upton Hiking Club

From: Upton Parks Department <info@uptonparks.org>

To: Arlo Gomes <arlog@uptonhikingclub.org>

Subject: RE: Hiking permits

Date: January 23

Attachment: Permit_Information_DRAFT

Hello, Mr. Gomes,

Thank you for your e-mail. I apologize that our Web site has not yet been updated with the information you were searching for and that the article in the Upton Digest was not clear. I have attached a proposed list of the twelve trails that will require permits and the number of permits that will be issued per day for each trail. The list will be finalized next month.

Permits can be reserved up to two weeks in advance, and the number of permits available for most trails is substantially higher than the number of Upton Hiking Club members who join your group hikes. Same-day permits can be obtained.

If you have not already done so, you can sign up on our Web site for our weekly newsletter. Doing so will ensure that you get advance notice of any updates to our policies.

Jenny Grieb, Public Relations, Upton Parks Department
